heading: বাংলাদেশের স্বাধীনতা : কূটনৈতিক যুদ্ধ
content_markdown:
৪৬০	বাংলাদেশের স্বাধীনতা : কূটনৈতিক যুদ্ধ

prevails at present on the borders of East Pakistan as a result of unprovoked and large-scale attacks by the Indian armed forces. As Your Excellency is aware, while accepting your office of good offices I had proposed a simultaneous withdrawal of Indian and Pakistani forces and suggested that may be supervised by UN. Obviate a threat to peace and to arrest the deteriorating situation, I now request Your Excellency to consider stationing a force of UN. observers on violations of our territory.

General Agha Muhammad Yahya Khan
Presedent of Pakistan.
Ends"

৫৯. জাতিসংঘ ডকুমেন্টে, Report of UN Secretary, General Relaling to situation in East Pakistan to the Security Council, S/10410, December 1971.

৬০. American Secret Documents, Foreings Relations 1969-1976, Volvot XI, South Asia Crisis, 1971, p. 24-25, Minutes of Senior Review Group Meeting/1, National Archives, Nixon Presidential Materials, NSC Files, California.

৬১. বাংলাদেশের স্বাধীনতা যুদ্ধ দলিলপত্র, ত্রয়োদশ খণ্ড, পৃ: ৮৬৯-৮৭০।

৬২. Bangladesh Documents, Vol. ii, P.219, সাধারণ পরিষদের সভাপতি জনাব আদম মালিক সংবাদ সম্মেলনে এ-সম্পর্কিত এক মন্তব্যে মানবিক কারণ’কে বড় করে দেখেছেন এবং শান্তিপূর্ণ উপায়ে দু'দেশের সমস্যা সমাধানে ভারতের প্রধানমন্ত্রী ও পাকিস্তানের প্রেসিডেন্টের নিকট আবেদন করেন।

৬৩. Bangladesh Documents, Vol. II, p. 489-90. পেরুর প্রতিনিধি প্রথম খসড়া প্রস্তাবে বলেন, "To cope with the effects and ignore the cause is a half-measure" পরের সংশোধনীতে বলেন, First cease-fire and at a subsequent stage adoption of measures to deal with the questions that have led to the outbreak of hostilities."

৬৪. Bangladesh Documents, Vol. II, p. 516. "There is a battle between Indian soldiers and Pakistani soldiers brought about by Pakistani aggression, and a battle between the Mukti Bahini and Pakistan soldiers brought about by Pakistani repression. What this draft resolution tends to do is to stop one kind of battle and leave the repression part, resistance part alone. This obviously will not work."

৬৫. UN Doc, S/10415. At the heart of these developments lies the war which has been waged since 25 March 1971 by the Government of Pakistan against 75 million people of Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan. Despite the full reports which have been appearing in the international press regarding this neighbouring territiories of India and consequent international tension, the United Nations had not addressed itself so far to this basic problem, nor has it so far taken into account the party most concerned in this tragic and dangerous crisis namely, the 75 million people of Bangla Desh. There can be no proper evalution of the present situation, its causes, present state and furture solution, without Bangla Desh being given a hearing.
